title: Unique extension from a single étale henselization stage
statement: Let B,C,A be commutative rings in one universe, J an ideal of B, f:B→C an étale ring map inducing an isomorphism B/J→C/JC, and (A,I) a henselian pair. For every ring map φ:B→A with J.map φ ≤ I, there exists exactly one ring map τ:C→A satisfying τ∘f=φ.

source.place: Tag 0A02, final paragraph; single-stage existence and uniqueness before passing to the colimit

proof.text: Form D = A tensor_B C using the algebra structures induced by φ and f. Étale base change makes D étale over A. The quotient isomorphism B/J → C/JC, base changed to A/I, gives A/I → D/ID an isomorphism. Its inverse yields the reduced section.

Henselianness gives I in the Jacobson radical and the monic coprime-factorization criterion. For a Gabber polynomial, lift its reduced factorization X^n times (X-1). The lifted second factor is monic linear, hence X-α with α-1 in I; this gives the root condition (if A/I is zero the radical condition forces A zero). Apply the Gabber section-lifting theorem to the inverse quotient section, then restrict the lifted A-algebra section along C → D.

For uniqueness, split the multiplication section D tensor_A D → D by an idempotent e, applying the étale-section splitting theorem over D. Its kernel is generated by 1-e. Two A-algebra sections of D agree modulo I because A/I → D/ID is surjective. Their tensor-pair map therefore sends e to an idempotent congruent to 1 modulo I. Idempotents determined modulo the Jacobson radical show that its value is 1. Thus the pair map kills the multiplication kernel, including x tensor 1 minus 1 tensor x. The two sections agree on every x, so their restrictions to C agree. Conversely every extension C → A produces an A-algebra section of D by tensor-product universality.
